query_text: How do you create eye contact with someone with a lazy eye?

content.text:
If someone has a lazy eye/strabismus, **make eye contact with the eye that appears to be looking at you**—or more simply, look at **the bridge of their nose / between their eyes**. From their perspective, that usually reads as normal eye contact and avoids you visibly switching back and forth.

A few practical tips:

- **Don’t stare at or “track” the misaligned eye.** That can feel awkward or insulting.
- **Keep your gaze relaxed** around their eyes/upper face, like you would with anyone else.
- **Focus on the conversation**, not on figuring out which eye is “correct.”
- If you know them well and it genuinely matters, you can politely ask:  
  *“Is there a side you prefer people look toward when talking with you?”*

Most of the time, the best approach is: **look at their face naturally, treat them normally, and don’t make it a thing.**
